chunks: Sa'd ibn Abdillah narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Hadid and Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Najran and al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz ibn Abdillah, from Zurarah, who said:

Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: "When you say the Takbir at the beginning of your prayer after the Opening Takbir with twenty-one Takbirs, then you forget all the Takbir and do not say it, the first Takbir will suffice for you - for the Takbir of the entire prayer."
And as for what was narrated - Sa'd ibn Abdillah from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad ibn Uthman, from Ubayd Allah ibn Ali al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

He said: I asked him about a man who forgot to say the Takbir until he had entered into the prayer, so he said: "Was it not his intention to say the Takbir?" I said: "Yes." He said: "Then let him proceed in his prayer."
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if one forgets the opening Takbirs during prayer?
ai.summary: This passage from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* highlights the Shia juristic principle of *al-asl fi al-af'al al-ibaha* (the default is permissibility) and the leniency applied to *nasi* (forgetfulness) in ritual acts. It distinguishes between a specific omission of the twenty-one Takbirs, where the first suffices, and a general omission with preserved intention, where the prayer remains valid without repetition, reflecting the Imams' emphasis on the continuity of worship over rigid formalism in cases of error.
